items.title: Proper base change for sheaves of sets on topological spaces
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: In a cartesian square of topological spaces with the vertical map f proper, the lemma shows that the inverse image of the pushforward of a sheaf of sets equals the pushforward of the inverse image along the base change (statement lines 3142-3154). The proof is a reduction of the whole argument of the proper base change theorem to the case of sheaves of sets: it suffices to identify the stalk of the pushforward at a point with the sections over the fibre, and that identification is reduced to the zeroth degree case of the closed-subset cohomology lemma, whose first part works verbatim for sheaves of sets (proof lines 3156-3164). The claim is H2: the same reduction as the abelian case, with the recognition that the only input used is insensitive to the absence of a group structure, and the omitted details are bounded.
